section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: The analog tracks reuse the Analog Rytm MKII's voice design. The voice control records have the Rytm MKII's format (command/depth word, start and target bytes, mode nibble, rate exponent and mantissa). The cymbal oscillator banks use the Rytm's scale (43.62 units per Hz) and load the Rytm's CH/CB CLASSIC values. So Rytm voice research applies here and back. `[doc]` (inferred from the shared formats)

section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: Digital tracks: rendered on CPU #2, then handed over by mailbox and eDMA channel 47 to CPU #1, which mixes them and sends them to the SSI1 codec. This agrees with SyntHack's audio path above. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
text: An emulator now boots 1.42 with both CPUs (analog-emu: stage 1 the main screen with a stand-in for CPU #2, stage 2 CPU #2 running for real). It is the only Syntakt 1.42 emulator in the catalogue; SyntHack's Unicorn harness targets 1.41. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Bank store: two 8 MiB slots inside the old 16 MiB `/mods` reservation, metadata sectors at eMMC `0x02bffe00` and `0x033ffe00`; the legacy record at `0x03400000` is still read. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware). The first trial crashed every boot (I62).

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Filter table: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from `0x40040060` (508 poles, then a zero tail; indices up to 1023 are read). A mod window in that tail made BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles; core 1.7.2 bounds the index. `[hw]` (I63)

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Load: MAIN is about 88 % with a plain pattern and 91-92 % with three POLY voices; code fetched from DDR costs far more than its instruction count (I64). `[hw]` {synfact-chorus}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Load after the MAIN optimisation (owner's unit, OS 1.41, stock pattern, 2026-11-13/14): a minimal bank (System Info + Modulation Skip) reads 81 % MAIN, the full bank 86 % before and 83 % after the optimisation release; about 2 points sat in LFO3's per-block callback, about 1 in the stereo audio callbacks. The meter rounds to whole percent; at 48 kHz and 32-sample blocks one MAIN point is about 6.7 µs per block. `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Appended boot storage is wiped at startup: on OS 1.41 the storage appended after the MAIN image is cleared and reused once the early resident copy is done, so code placed there is gone when the application runs; only the resident reserve (64 KiB in Synfact's core) is safe for code called after boot (I104). `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Stock track types: every stock digital track type has bit 6 clear; Synfact's machines use types 64-79, so a mod can tell that all tracks are stock from the type bytes alone. The MAIN audio interrupt calls the stock modulation routine `0x40097afc` for every track on every block (about 6,600 emulated instructions for the full body). `[doc]` / `[emu]` {synfact-main-opt}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Build and voices: builds use `-mcpu=54415` (an MCF5441x part), SMZ bank code `-fno-jump-tables`. Each track has one stock voice block at `0x80000000 + t*0x708`; the stock voice reset rewrites +`0x570`-`0x708` and zeroes 48 bytes at the pointer in +`0x56c`. `[doc]` {synfact-machine-ref}

section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
text: Free memory, checked on a unit (2026-11-10): a probe machine (type 70, MEM PROBE) filled the shared-window gap `0x5b0..0x7df` (AUDIO `0x5b0`, MAIN `0x100005b0`) and the AUDIO SRAM tail `0x8000f398..0x8000ffff` (after FM TONE's scratch; the stock boot leaves it zero) with a pattern and checked it every block: nothing else wrote either area over several minutes. Synfact core 1.8 uses both for stereo tracks. `[hw]` {synfact-memprobe}

section: Syntakt / SY SWARM read from the audio program (model27 notes/84, OS 1.42 section 7, same in 1.41, 2026-11-16)
text: Engine 10 (SY SWARM): update `0x400092ec`, render `0x400096e8`. Seven sawtooths from band-limited tables, one per octave (`0x40006588` picks the table by note, `0x40006434` reads it with linear interpolation); a centre that SUB moves down 0, 1 or 2 octaves (its increment shifted right and its table picked again, nothing else), six detuned oscillators driven by six tables indexed by DET; ANIM is three slow sines (about 1, 2 and 5 Hz, `0x40006074`) that phase-modulate oscillator pairs in opposite directions; NMOD is a noise generator (`0x40003eb4`) that phase-modulates the six; MIX uses two gain tables; every oscillator gets a random phase at a trig. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / SY SWARM read from the audio program (model27 notes/84, OS 1.42 section 7, same in 1.41, 2026-11-16)
text: Its six detune tables equal Adam Szabo's published Super Saw model (his offsets times his 11th-degree detune polynomial, KTH 2010) to 0.000 cents over all 128 × 6 values; its mix curves are not his. `[doc]` (computed by model27, static reading)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Sequencer step per track (MAIN): the sequencer runs in a forced interrupt at `0x4008c924` (24 ticks a quarter note) for 13 tracks (12 = FX). Per track `t`: next step `0x43bd73fc+t`, step before `0x43bd7416+t`, ticks into the step `0x43bd7409+t`, steps toward the bar `0x43bd753c+t`. The step advances at `0x4008d0e4..0x4008d120`; length is the track's (track record `+969`, a word; record = pattern + `0x499*t`) when pattern byte `+0x21379` is set, else the pattern's (`+0x21374`). Trig preparation `0x4008b882` at tick 0 (call sites `0x4008cf00`, `0x4008cf14`; `0x4008c204` for a pattern started mid-way). UI copies `0x444e2370+t` (last) and `0x444e237d+t` (step), copied each tick at `0x4008d1a8`; live recording reads `0x444e2370`. `[doc]` / `[emu]` (Unicorn)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: The trig LEDs' playhead reads another copy: the accessor `0x4008b734(t)` (read by `0x400c20ee`). playhead-st build 2 reversed the sound on a unit, but the LED playhead still ran forwards until this accessor was patched too. `[hw]` (I116)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Pattern and kit pointers: playing pattern `0x43bd7430` with kit `0x43bd743c`, next `0x43bd7438` with `0x43bd7444`; live kits at `0x41ad5134 + k*0x1618`, k < 128. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Free tail in a kit slot: an encoded kit slot is `0x1600` bytes; the native codec uses `[0, 0x14d2)`, LFO3 `[0x14e0, 0x15d0)`, playhead-st `[0x15e0, 0x15f8)`. Stock never reads the tail, so a project saved with mod data there still opens on a stock unit. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Unsaved kit changes reach a power cycle only through the mirrors: a native kit edit ends in `KitActive::kitChanged` (`0x40172250`, vtable `0x401c33f4` +`0x5c`; object at `0x40a38b18 + 0x378d8`), which re-encodes the kit into its mirror slots (job at `0x4001082e`). Mod data written only on a project save came back after save + power cycle but not after a power cycle without save. `[hw]` (I116)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Key IDs beyond core-st's list: TRK = 2, UP = 14, DOWN = 15, LEFT = 16, RIGHT = 17. The MainScreen header (`0x40032b0e..0x40032b72`) draws the tempo right-aligned to x 125 and the metronome left of it, rows 55..62. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Naming (Synfact 2026-11-18): Synfact calls the object that `0x4016e044` returns the *root owner* and the native ViewController the object at root + `0x40`, whose dirty byte is at its + `0x20` (root + `0x60`); a redraw request written to root + `0x20` does nothing (Playhead 1.2 did this). Read "UI controller" below as Synfact's root owner. `[emu]` {synfact-1119}

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: View manager (UI controller +`0x40`): list sentinel +`0x14`, tail +`0x18`, highest opaque node +`0x1c`; a node holds its view at +`0x8`; a view's closed flag is a byte at +`0x30`. Native close `0x400ffd02` sets it and requests deferred cleanup (manager +`0x22`); it does not destroy the view, and a shared owner can keep it alive after removal. Push `0x40100bc2` calls visibility `0x40100ade` before the new view's attach callback; visibility composes the UI synchronously (`0x4000a0e6`) and runs mod tick code. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: Stock deferred cleanup drops a close raised during composition: cleanup `0x40100ea4` clears manager +`0x22` at `0x40100f2c..0x40100f3e` after the visibility call, so a close requested by a tick inside that call is lost and the closed view stays in the list (key walks skip it but nothing removes it). Synfact core 1.8.2 moves the clear before the call. Mods that close views from tick code are exposed. `[emu]` (reproduced; the related unit symptom is I115)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: MainScreen children: MainScreen show `0x40033b74` publishes, in order, `+0x228`, the current parameter view `+0xc0`, `+0xe8`, `+0x218`, `+0xf0`, `+0x220`, so the parameter view is normally not the stack tail; permanent mute is a separate transparent child at `+0x230`. The stock LED setter `0x40008220` keeps the first write per LED. The native TRIG key advances the page index on release. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
text: MAIN mixer call: `0x400a4fce` calls `0x4008f1ca` with three stack words (the third is the mixer record); its frame is 556 bytes. The tail `0x4008fb38` combines ADC `0x8000ded0` with the preview bus `0x8000dfd0` and runs USB and codec output; six 256-byte buses start at `0x8000dad0`. Native transport STOP is `0x4008c288`. `[emu]` (analog-emu interpreter)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Stock builds one sample blob in MAIN DDR at boot: the native builder (`0x400822bc` on 1.41, `0x40082334` on 1.42) reads each of the 64 stock slots through a temporary 512 KiB buffer and concatenates them at physical `0x4584f2c5` (used through the uncached alias `0x4d84f2c5`; same address on both OS versions): 64 `u32` frame counts, then 2 bytes per mono frame, no 64-byte SAMP header; an empty slot still takes its 4-byte count. With 64 five-second slots it is 30,720,256 bytes (29.30 MiB) and ends at `0x4759b3c5` (exclusive). The stock sender (`0x40082f90` on 1.42) then copies it in 2,048-byte pages through the mailbox at `0x10000800`; CPU #2 keeps its own copy. `[emu]` (Unicorn running each OS's own builder with file and heap stand-ins)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: So `0x45565490-0x48000000` is unsafe from about `0x4584f2c5` up: past 8,064,315 bytes of blob (84.000625 s of mono 48 kHz PCM16 in all, for example 17 five-second samples) it reaches `0x46000000`; in the reproduction the first overlapping write came from stock's memcpy (`0x40115f94` on 1.41, `0x40116158` on 1.42) while copying slot 17. This is the mechanism behind SyntHack's lesson at `0x46000000` (I20) and also covers SY FM4's `0x47000000`. Limiting each slot to 5 s does not keep it out. `[emu]` / `[hw]` (I145)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: CPU #2 reads the stock pool at `0x4004f750`: its receiver (`0x40000fba`) and descriptor parser (`0x40000d06`) use that base, unchanged from 1.41 to 1.42 (section 7 is identical). Synfact's 1.42 port first moved the base to `0x4004f7c8` by mistake; core 2.0.1 restores it. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Stock per-slot limit as Synfact checks it: one sector per stock header, a SAMP header and at most 240,000 mono frames (5 s); a slot's on-disk body is at most 480,064 bytes (64-byte header plus PCM). All 64 full slots are 15,001 sender pages. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: Synfact core 2.0.1 streams instead: it no longer calls the stock builder; it plans the 64 slots from their headers and builds each sender page on demand from eMMC (byte-identical to the old blob), using 5,120 bytes of MAIN scratch freed by a task-only hook at `0x40083026` after the last mailbox copy. Waveform envelopes are read lazily (at most 4,096 PCM bytes per UI idle call); the cache is about 98 KiB for 128 entries, allocated on first use. The native heap is 16 MiB, too small for a 29.3 MiB blob anyway. Resident use: 65,116 of 65,536 bytes (420 free). `[emu]` (sender, page and parser code run in Unicorn); boot with 64 five-second samples `[hw]` (prototype, owner's unit)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: OS 1.42 versus 1.41 (MAIN): build id 0097 (1.41: 0094); MAIN decoded 3,442,576 bytes (3,438,480); container 2,029,392 bytes (2,028,880), plus 94 transport-padding bytes in the .syx; SRAM copy source end `0x40348b90` (`0x40347b90`); BSS clear end `0x45566490` (`0x45565490`); boot stack `0x48000000` on both. MAIN SHA-256 `1a9723b1...eb3e7`. Sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 (bootstrap, updater and AUDIO included) are byte-identical; section 5 and the container header change. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
text: No single offset from 1.41 to 1.42: code and tables moved by `+0x78`, `+0xac`, `+0x1c4`, `+0x29c`, `+0x2a0`, `+0x320` or `+0x354`; the DDR image and BSS by `+0x1000`. Synfact found its 108 sites with masked byte-pattern contexts and then checked each one. Examples (1.41 -> 1.42): draw-all `0x401007ce` -> `0x40100992`; operator new `0x40103788` -> `0x4010394c`; menu item ctor `0x400fa688` -> `0x400fa84c`; menu add `0x400f9ebe` -> `0x400fa082`; app startup site `0x400826a6` -> `0x4008271e`; mixer call `0x400a4fce` -> `0x400a5046` (calls `0x4008f1ca` -> `0x4008f242`); modulation `0x40097afc` -> `0x40097b74`; LFO `0x40119266` -> `0x4011942a`; deferred view cleanup's clear `0x40100f2c` -> `0x401010f0`; trig preparation `0x4008b882` -> `0x4008b8fa`. Key and encoder dispatch (`0x4000839e`, `0x400083f0`) and the vector-base routine `0x40001d28` did not move. `[doc]` (G5 anchor data)

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)

section: Syntakt / Syntakt Performance Mods: PERFORM filter on the analog FX block (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-16/17)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: How the peer CPU gets its program: MAIN reads ids 6 and 7 from the OS directory in NOR (`0x80000`, "ELE3", 16-byte entries from `0x80020`: id, offset, length) and streams them at every boot over DSPI2 (`0xEC038000`) in slave mode, eDMA channel 29 one byte per request. Buffers are `0xAA | big-endian length | payload`: id 6 at `0x4f8af2c1` after eight `0xFF` bytes (MAIN changes byte 1 from `0x01` to `0x0f`), id 7 at `0x4f84f2c1` (length limit `0x5fffb`, matching SY FM4's "0x60000 - 5"). Section 6 (stage 1, SRAM `0x80000000`) sets up DDR, takes the stream and jumps through `*(0x40000400)`. Who starts DSPI0 as master before stage 1 is open. `[doc]` (stream bytes `[emu]`: payload equals section 7 by SHA-256)

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Two pins form the handshake: MAIN's doorbell (GPIO port A bit 4) is the peer's DTIM0 capture event (vector 96); the peer's pin (port 6 bit 2: set via `0xEC09401E`, cleared via `0xEC09402A`) is MAIN's EPORT IRQ4 (vector 68). Peer steps the window state `+8` from 1 to `0xC` (hello "HO"/"HA" at `+0/+2`, `0xA5A5` at `+4`, window RAM test with `0xAAAAAAAA`/`0x55555555`, sample chunks), then installs its frame handler `0x40000934`. MAIN status `0x41bbf448` and state `0x41bb32b0` reach 6. Without a peer, "DSP BOOT FAILURE (TIMEOUT)" follows after `0x12` poll periods (about 1.04 G emulated instructions). `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: MAIN mixes the digital voices and owns the audio clock: eDMA ch 54 (TCD `0xFC0456C0`) streams a 2 KB ring at SRAM `0x80000000` (64 frames x 8 words) to the SSI TX FIFO `0xFC0C8000`; its half-way interrupt is the 1500 Hz audio frame (32 samples at 48 kHz, SSI1 slave; vector 174, handler `0x400a2058`). That handler forces INTC1 source 63 to run the engine tick (vector 191, `0x400a38ce`, 7,550 bytes), which mixes the 8 voices from `0x80003d50` in Q31 and fills the other half. Main L/R sit in ring words 5 and 3 as 24-bit signed (the Q31 mix shifted right by 8). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: Frame budget numbers (emulator): MAIN needs about 117,000 instructions per frame; the peer's frame handler about 86,500 idle and up to 88,900 with a note. digikit runs MAIN at 189.9 M instructions/s (264 MHz core over a measured busy CPI of 1.39); at one instruction per 132 MHz bus tick (88,000 per frame) MAIN did not fit. The peer's hottest code is the voice oscillator `0x4000290e` (98 instructions, 18 call sites, 21-24 % of the frame handler). `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
text: The top 4 MiB of DDR is a ring: `0x400966e0` memsets 4 MiB at uncached `0x4fc00000` at boot; `0x4009687a` and `0x4009748c` index it as `0x4fc00000 + 8*(i & 0x7ffff)`, advance by `0x20` per frame and hand it to eDMA. So cached `0x47c00000..0x48000000` is cleared at every boot and written every frame (that it is the delay memory is open; SyntHack called `0x4FC00000` delay/reverb lines on 1.41). digikit's first `cf.expansion` (`0x47e8b000..0x47fe0000`) sat inside it and was moved. `[doc]` (O35)

section: Syntakt / Upgrade receiver, transport state, native bitmaps (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18)
text: Native Bitmap API (1.42 MAIN): constructor `0x400f72be(object, width, height, pixels, mask)`, clipped rectangle fill `0x400f7fb6`, masked blit `0x400f8f70(dst, src, x, y, flags)`; an eight-word object can borrow pixel and mask arrays with no heap allocation. A 128 x 64 bitmap is 256 big-endian words per array, two words per column; y = 0 is bit 31 of the first word, y = 63 bit 0 of the second; a zero mask bit keeps the destination pixel. This is the bitmap layer; the panel's own row order is a different layer (compare D13). `[emu]` (executed in Unicorn) {synfact-1119}

text: Power-off save: the power-sense interrupt (`0x40001d88`, PPDSDR_C bit 2, as on the Rytm) forces INTC1 source 30; its handler `0x40001d5e` calls `0x400bcf7a`, which writes the COKI working state to sectors `0x7a000`/`0x7c000` only when byte `0x43be3154` is set, else it only parks the card. `0x400bd8a0` sets that byte once PPDSDR_G bit 3 (supercap charged) reads high; the Rytm's signal is PPDSDR_A bit 5. section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: AUDIO image layout (traced from section 7's code, `tools/study_st_audio_memory.py`): entry word at `0x40000400` (-> `0x40001070`), code `0x40000404-0x40009f1c` (11,477 instructions reached), tables to `0x40040850`; `0x40040860-0x40041050` is zero in stock (Synfact's AUDIO services sit there); the packed FPGA stream at `0x40041060` unpacks to `0x40042000`. The image tail `0x4004f6e0-0x4005df10` holds SRAM's initial contents (copied to `0x80000000` and `0x80008000` at boot). VBR is `0x40000000` (the value is stored at `0x4004005c`); boot points all 256 vectors at an `rte`, then sets vector 96 and the block interrupt. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: The sample-page receiver has a forbidden page: MAIN writes a 16-bit page index at window `0x00c` and 2 KiB at `0x800`; AUDIO copies to `0x4004f750 + index * 0x800` with no bound. Index `0x8000` lands on `0x4404f750-0x4404ff50`, AUDIO's own variables and 64-entry sample table: never send it. Indices `0x8001-0xffff` reach `0x4404ff50-0x4804f750`, which runs past the stack top; keep pages below `0x47ff0000`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Nothing in the stock AUDIO image names an address above `0x4404f980` (the end of the zeroed data, named once by the clear; no allocator). The AUDIO stack starts at `0x48000000`, the main context idles and all work runs in the block interrupt: at most 3,140 bytes deep by static count. ACR0 `0x4007e020` caches `0x40000000-0x47ffffff`, so AUDIO has 128 MiB as MAIN does. That nothing writes the high zone at run time is not yet shown on a unit (Synfact's high-memory probe, type 70, is built for that check). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Stock MAIN cost (emulator profile with a calibrated cache model, default project in PLAY, not meter readings): the block routine `0x400a38ce` is 97.5 % of MAIN's instructions. Per block about 72,400 instructions, 1,466 I-cache misses and 206 D-cache misses, modelled as 77 % of a 250 MHz MAIN; stopped gives nearly the same. About 22 KB of code runs every block against an 8 KB, 4-way, 16-byte-line I-cache, so almost every hot line misses once per block: 1 KB less code per block is about 1.5 MAIN points, 1,000 fewer instructions about 0.5. The model (cycles ~ 0.85 x instructions + 40 x misses) was fitted on a unit for AUDIO code and predicted the first Chorus port's jump from 88 % to 100 %. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Hot stock MAIN routines (1.42): mixer `0x4008f242` (8.8 %), reverb `0x40096eb4` (7.9 %, hand-written EMAC), block body `0x400a38ce` (6.2 %), smoothing of 938 16-bit parameters `0x400979ca` (4.1 %, then a 1,612-byte copy), LFO `0x4011942a` (3.3 %), delay `0x40096908` (2.6 %), modulation group `0x40097b24` (51 calls a block). Mix kernels for 8, 9 and 10 tracks: `0x4008f0b6`, `0x4008f024`, `0x4008ef8c`; when no gain ramps, their per-frame increment adds and store-back do nothing. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Cache control: stock MAIN has a single `movec cacr`, at boot (`0x4000055a`, value `0xa50ce100`: I- and D-cache, store buffer and branch cache on). The MCF5441x can lock I-cache ways 0-1 with `CACR[IHLCK]` (RM 6.4.5); any later write of `0xa40ce100` (the invalidate that mods use after changing code) also drops the lock. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Native project workers (1.42 MAIN): each project command loads its worker's address with a `move.l #imm,d0` at a fixed site: new `0x4005d83a` (worker `0x40059f9e`), rename `0x4005a486` (`0x4005a6f8`), copy `0x4005a558` (`0x4005a788`), paste `0x4005a606` (`0x4005a7aa`), clear `0x4005a6a6` (`0x4005a7d0`), clear selected `0x4005d20e` (`0x4005a828`), delete selected `0x4005d3b6` (`0x4005a8a2`), save `0x4005b662` (`0x4005ba50`), load `0x4005d9dc` (`0x4005bafa`). Autosave and project SysEx do not go through them. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
text: Native three-pane list (1.42 MAIN): constructor `0x400fad82`, draw `0x400faa2e`, base painter `0x400f572c` (rows start 6 px above the viewport top, 8 more for a titled pane); item constructor `0x400fa84c` takes a draw callback `(capture, item, bitmap, x, y)` that runs before the selection XOR; small-font lookup `0x400f9478(view+0x94)`. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: FX-bus VCA gains on 1.42: the two FX VCA gains sit in D1/D3 at `0x400905b6` (stock bytes `0c81 0000 ffff`, a clamp compare); the native clamp and stores run through `0x400905da` and write hardware context +70/+72 (decimal). The 1.41 site was `0x4009053e`. Changing only these two gains there compresses whatever reaches the FX track, after DRIVE and filter, and leaves direct track outputs and the MAIN mix alone. At this site the native MOVCLR leaves ACC0/ACC1 empty; a callback may use them but must keep ACC2/ACC3. `[doc]` (site and stores compared with stock 1.42); comp-st 0.2.0 using it reported working on the owner's unit `[hw]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: FX ADC pair: the detector input for the FX bus is fixed at `0x80003c50` and `0x80003cd0`, 32 signed Q31 frames each (the ADC 6/7 capture SyntHack named on 1.41). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: The digital FX bus is not the whole FX input: `0x8000dad0` (Synfact's `ST_FX_TRACK_BUS`, the first of the six mixer buses) is the digital bus before the analog FX block. Processing it digitally does not cover what the analog circuit routes to FX; for that, detect on the ADC pair and act on the VCAs. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: Kit pointers and codecs on 1.42: live kits at `0x41ad6134 + k*0x1618`, k < 128 (1.41: `0x41ad5134`, the `+0x1000` DDR shift). `KitActive::kitChanged` is `0x40172414` (vtable `0x401c3694` +`0x5c`; object `0x40a713f0`, kits at its +`0x10`). Native Kit new `0x400b3384`, encode `0x400a78f4`, decode `0x400a78a0`; native memcpy `0x4011613c`; the global Kit model's has/get/set start at `0x4000d870`, `0x4000d94a`, `0x4000da32`. Core 2.4 takes these sites once and passes notifications to modules, so Chorus and LFO3 no longer patch them themselves. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: Kit slot tail, 1.42: native `[0, 0x14d2)`, LFO3 `[0x14e0, 0x15d0)`, comp-st `[0x15d0, 0x15e0)` (tag `0x4351`, six big-endian Q8 words, a 16-bit check), playhead-st `[0x15e0, 0x15f8)`; the tail is now full up to `0x15f8`. The native Kit SysEx uses a shorter layout, so tail data does not travel in a Kit SysEx dump. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: Compressor cost in Synfact's emulator (guest instructions per 32-frame block, not cycles): the Digitakt mk1 compressor ported literally would cost about 2,900-3,050 for the gain calculation alone; SyntHack's compact master-comp core 98 off, 564-611 on; comp-st 0.2.0 in the full bank 43 off, 377-379 below threshold, 484-509 compressing, against Chorus at about 2,180-4,040. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
text: Profile of the real shipped bank (analog-emu with a patch that forces the 1.42 profile for a modified image): the per-block hot code is the stock audio block; the mods' code shows almost no cache misses. With an 8 KB I-cache against about 22 KB of code per block, any lock set covers at most about 16-19 %, so a better lock set than icache-lock-st's cannot recover much. The MAIN parameter smoother keeps its arrays in SRAM (uncached) and runs with `MACSR=0x28`; its one-pole has a history-dependent dead band, so "converged" is not one value. Only an A/B on the unit (same core, banks differing by one module) measures real CPU. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Two images boot on the unit: `device-peer` (only the section 7 packer below) and, after the repair below, the full `device` set (runtime, DIGIKIT menu, HEALTH, input, card guard, section 7 packer). The second CPU loads the unpacked section 7, the store works and a content module (digikit/remote) was installed from the workbench, selected, applied and ran with working keys. `[hw]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The patched image did not fit without packing section 7: Elektron stores section 7 raw (383,760 B, SHA-256 `daf6451c...ec783bc2`); with it raw the patched container was 2,129,312 B, 32,672 B over the 2 MiB upgrade limit (`0x1FFE00`). Packed (aPLib with an 8-byte header: big-endian body length and byte sum) it is 264,194 B. The full set with the guard is 2,079,872 B (16.4 KB free). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: How MAIN reads section 7 (no stage buffer): the peer thread (entry `0x40082c04`, made by `0x40082e9c` from the boot thread) loads A2 with the NOR read `0x40116d7a` (6-byte `lea` at `0x40082c24`), reads id 6 into `0x4f8af2c9` and id 7 straight into the transmit buffer at `0x4f84f2c6` (`0xAA` at `0x4f84f2c1`, big-endian length at `0x4f84f2c2`). The only length check is `length + 5 <= 0x60000` at `0x40082d66` (else "DSP BOOT FAILURE (BUF)"); a missing id gives status 1 at `0x40082e84`. No other code reads id 7; the bootstrap and the OS-upgrade receiver do not parse sections. The handshake timeout (about 5.1 s, 19 polls) starts only after both NOR reads and the DMA arm, so unpacking before the stream costs no timeout time. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: digikit's peer-image hook: it replaces that `lea` so id 7 is read to the end of the buffer, checked (length, byte sum), unpacked forward with the firmware's own depacker `0x401181ec` (no output bound; returns the length in D0) and checked again (length, SHA-256 of the stock section). On any failure it takes the missing-section path: the second CPU gets no bytes and MAIN shows "OOPS! SOMETHING WENT WRONG, SWITCH OFF/ON TO BOOT AGAIN." The in-place margin of the packed stream is 9,444 B. Boot cost estimate 0.25-0.4 s (not measured on the unit). `[emu]` (proof with a one-byte-changed stream refused) / `[hw]` (boots)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The second CPU must get the exact stock bytes: section 7 carries a second FPGA bitstream (at `0x40041060`) that the peer loads through its own DSPI. MAIN configures the main FPGA itself from section 1: `0x400bd74e` reads id 1, unpacks it with `0x401181ec` to `0x43be315c` (length at `0x43be3158`, 149,516 B), and `0x400bcb4e` shifts it out over DSPI `0xFC03C000` after INIT goes high. This corrects the earlier "the bootstrap configures the FPGA" (section list above). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Bootstrap stage and in-place unpack: the Syntakt bootstrap copies packed MAIN to `0x40200000` and unpacks it in place to `0x40000400` (depacker `0x8000041c`; stage constant at `0x800005b2`, `0x800005d2`, `0x80000622`, `0x8000155c`, `0x8000157e`). It checks no bound and no checksum; when the output overtakes the unread stream the decoder runs away and MAIN never starts. Margins at this stage: stock +96,356 B, `device-peer` +67,676 B, the first full `device` image -42,486 B (it hung the unit, I183). digikit now refuses a margin under 8 KiB and writes the stream's last tokens as literals to reach it. The emulator had missed it because it installs MAIN directly and never runs the bootstrap's unpack. `[hw]` (hang) / `[doc]` (stage, margins) (I183, compare SyntHack's padded build above)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Key ids in key events differ from the Digitakt II/Digitone II: the id at +`0xc` of a key event is the firmware key index from the decoder table `0x401d7a48`: YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17, LEVEL push 48 (a second YES key in lists; the stock compact menu handler `0x400f5c82` treats 12 and `0x30` alike). On DT2/DN2 the same keys are 10, 12, 15 and 49. The flag bits look the same: bit 0 set on a press (cursor keys and RIGHT act on it), bit 4 on a release (YES acts on it). `[doc]` (I181)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The card capacity is a driver word: the eSDHC init (`0x4010ebea`, boot thread) stores the capacity in sectors at `0x444ba720` (from EXT_CSD SEC_COUNT, else the CSD); the 20-byte getter `0x4010f232` returns it, or `0xFFFFFFFF` while the driver is not ready (same hash on DT2 1.17 `0x4012ddd6`, DN2 1.12 `0x4012c49a`, DN2 1.11 `0x4012c1ba`). The part table (7 rows of 32 bytes at `0x402d5adc`) is checked at boot but not enforced on the Syntakt: only the self-test reads the result (the DT2 gates its mount on it). Only the self-test makes the pSLC (enhanced area) conversion. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: One unit's card: INFO reports `0x3a4000` sectors (1.82 GiB): the `4FTE4R` part with the enhanced area set, the smallest capacity in the table. So do not assume the 32 GB `0x2e1a000` part the emulators model. `[hw]` (I182)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: What stock touches on the card: nothing is sized from the capacity. FORMAT +DRIVE erases `0x80000-0x17ffff` and `0x1000-0x1fff` (with SAMPLES also `0x2000-0x11fff`), not the whole card; stock 1.42 touches only sectors below `0x180000`. digikit's Syntakt store is now the fixed area `0x200000-0x300000` (1-1.5 GiB, 512 MiB): 256 MiB above the last stock sector and below the smallest listed capacity. Store writes, listing and removal worked on the unit. `[doc]` / `[hw]` (store)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The eMMC write and erase entries: block write `0x4010f7f8` `(sector, bytes, buf)` and block erase `0x4010f52a` `(sector, count)` are the only MAIN code that writes or erases the user area, except the OS-upgrade finale's raw controller writes of the COKi copies (`0x400bcf7a`) and the CMD6 EXT_CSD writes in `0x4010f3d8` (one-time-programmable card setup: never call it). The write splits requests over 64 KiB by calling itself (return address entry + `0x36`) and is bounded only by the capacity; the erase checks nothing, and a count of 0 makes the end sector `sector - 1`. Both start with 8 bytes of `lea; movem.l` (no PC-relative operand); D0, D1, A0, A1 and the flags are dead at both entries; same hash and size on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12 and 1.11. Five 1.42 callers ignore the result (the console command `0x40080646`, the COKi writer `0x400bcadc`, the Data API Clear `0x400b639a`, the COKi restore `0x400bd608` twice). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: digikit's card write guard (built for the Syntakt, emulator only): `before` hooks at both entries refuse a request outside the row of its writer class (stock: `[0, 0x180000)`; the runtime's own write, known by its return address: the store) and return -10, the driver's own out-of-range code, before any lock is taken. The Data API then reports "Failed to write to eMMC". It cannot see the finale's raw writes or CMD6. The guard is on in both Syntakt sets; no refusal was reported from the unit. `[emu]` (SB35)

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Hook sites found by hash on 1.42 (not checked on this image, `[?]`): project slot setter `0x4006f2ce`, slot byte `0x40653441`, save exit `0x4001a7d4`, clear-one exit `0x4005a81a`, clear-many exit `0x4005a898`, paste exit `0x400c2116`; USB EP0 setup dispatcher `0x400062e2`, EP0 send `0x4000621c`, setup packet `0x454e4bdc`. `[?]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Recovery path digikit gives: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), the stock file over 5-pin MIDI DIN; back up the +Drive card first and do not put samples or sounds into the stock slots with Transfer until the Data API guard exists. Whether the logo-hung unit came back through that menu is not stated. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Size baseline 2026-11-22: digikit's `device` set now stores 2,102,528 B against its cap of 2,096,640 B (`0x1FFE00`), 5,888 B over, after the 2026-11-21 set that booted on the unit was 2,079,872 B; growth on the development lane. About 69.8 KB of MAIN's tail is stored as literals because the unpack margin is small; the DIGIKIT menu (19,104 B stored) is to move to the card first. Measured with patchkit; nothing flashed. `[doc]` {digikit-1122}

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The in-place unpack sets a hard floor on stored MAIN (finding 159, static): the room before the output reaches the stream start is `0x200000 - 0x400` = 2,096,128 B. Since only literals keep the slack constant, the binding point is the end of the stream: stored MAIN >= unpacked MAIN - 2,096,128 + margin floor + 8 (header). Checked against the hung image of I183: 3,683,064 B out, 1,544,457 B plain stream, -42,486 B margin (formula: -42,471). Stock MAIN is 3.44 MB; digikit's appended runtime is 274,498 B (was 215,583). `[doc]` {digikit-1123} ([I183](../INCIDENTS.md#i183-a-full-digikit-image-hung-a-syntakt-at-the-logo-the-bootstraps-unpack-overran-its-stream))

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: What follows for a Syntakt mod: each byte removed from unpacked MAIN saves one stored byte (not the about 0.54 the packer ratio suggests). Moving bytes around, splitting the stream, packer depth or choosing which bytes become literals cannot go below the floor; they only choose where the padding sits. digikit's 111,517 B literal tail costs 69,762 B because the plain stream was that far short of the floor. Only a smaller MAIN, a lower margin or code outside MAIN's stream helps. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: The 8 KiB margin floor is a safety default, not a measurement: `main_margin_min` = 8192 in digikit's device data. If the depacker `0x8000041c` reads one byte at a time (read once, a second check is wanted), a slack of 0 or more after each token would do; a word prefetch would need 4 or more. Lowering the floor to 64 B would save 8,128 B. digikit plans this only as a fallback, after a second read of the loop and a run of the real bootstrap depacker on the exact stream (`depack_check`, length and SHA-256). Too low a floor hangs the unit at the logo ([I183](../INCIDENTS.md#i183-a-full-digikit-image-hung-a-syntakt-at-the-logo-the-bootstraps-unpack-overran-its-stream)). `[doc]` (open) {digikit-1123}

section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
text: Other room for code: section 8 (103 KB stored, use unknown) and a section 4 repack are read-only for patchkit, with unknown consumers; whether the bootstrap walks a table of section ids and accepts an unknown one is unread. Code caves give only about 2 KB. The OS-upgrade stage (`0x403d10d0`) lies above and is not used at boot. `[doc]` / `[?]` (section 8, unknown ids) {digikit-1123}

section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
text: A redraw request recomposes the whole screen: the UI is double-buffered and every repaint redraws all visible views; the COMP page alone costs about 30,000 instructions per recompose. With drums, comp-st 0.2.0's GR meter asked for a repaint on 24-26 of the 30 UI ticks a second, and MAIN rose on the unit with the page open ([I196](../INCIDENTS.md#i196-a-compressors-gr-meter-raised-main-cpu-through-screen-repaints-synfact-comp-st-020-syntakt)). 0.3 repaints for the meter at most every third tick (10 Hz) and ignores 1-pixel moves except to zero: 8-10 a second with drums, none with a steady signal. The drop on the unit is not measured. `[hw]` (symptom) / `[emu]` (counts) {synfact-1123}

section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
text: The AUDIO chain's multimode is one load away from replaceable: the stock chain loads its per-track multimode routine with `lea 0x400019d6,a4` at `0x40000a72`; core 2.5 changes it to `movea.l 0x40040f3c,a4` (chain directory word 3, which holds `0x400019d6` until a bank writes its own entry). The native routine's first part `0x400019d6-0x40001ea3` has no PC-relative operand and no call, and every exit joins at `0x40001ea4`, so it can be copied and run elsewhere. samplers-st copies it on the unit from its own AUDIO image only when the bytes match 1.42's fingerprint. `[doc]` {synfact-1123}

text: COMP's sidechain filter (SCF): a one-pole high-pass on the detector only, `lp += a(x - lp)`, `y = x - lp`, `a = 1 - exp(-2 pi fc / 48000)`, state in ACC0/ACC1 during the block; OFF plus 127 cutoffs log-spaced from 60 Hz to 1 kHz. Extra instructions per block: 43 with MIX at 0, 395-397 below threshold and 502-528 compressing with SCF off, 600 and 705-738 with SCF at 150 Hz; every cutoff costs the same. A 50 Hz kick is 3.8 dB lower to the detector at 60 Hz and 14.0 dB at 250 Hz. The position is stored in RAT's unused low byte; a 0.2.0 bank refuses such a Kit and restores COMP's defaults. Synfact does not trust Unicorn for EMAC arithmetic and checks the loop in analog-emu's cfbench (2,688 blocks against a 64-bit model). `[emu]` {synfact-1123}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt SysEx: pattern locks and the project file protocol (OS 1.42, 2026-11-22/23)
text: Pattern dump and lock IDs: the 0x61 pattern dump is 27,136 bytes (build 0097). Measured lock IDs: 28 FLTR FREQ, 29 RESO, 39-43 AMP ATK/HOLD/DEC/SUS/REL, 44 delay send, 45 reverb send, 46 PAN (raw/256 - 64), 47 VOL, 49 envelope mode (high byte, ADSR = 1). An ID belongs to the parameter, not to the knob position. Values are 16-bit big-endian, display x 256 (the low byte is the fine part). Lock records are kept sorted by ID; deleting a trig clears its records; a single-trig delete leaves the step word 0x0000, CLEAR SEQUENCE leaves 0x0380. `[hw]` {digi-roll-1124}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt SysEx: pattern locks and the project file protocol (OS 1.42, 2026-11-22/23)
text: Project files over SysEx: Elektron's SysEx RPC frames are `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`, 7-bit packed data, `F7`; a reply carries the request's counter and opcode with the high bit set. `/projects` holds slots 1-128. Reads are open, partial reads (2048-byte chunks, CRC-32 each, about 20 KB/s) and close; writes go in chunks of up to 32,768 bytes and each reply reports the byte count so far. The unit decompresses and recompresses a written project, so a check must compare decoded contents. A slot read matched Transfer's backup byte for byte. `[hw]` {synpat-1124}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt SysEx: pattern locks and the project file protocol (OS 1.42, 2026-11-22/23)
text: Project file: a `.stprj` is a ZIP with `manifest.json` and one payload: a 31-byte header (magic, project version, slot, decompressed size), LZ4 blocks and a CRC-32 trailer; the image is about 4 MB with 128 patterns and 128 kits at fixed offsets. Project versions 0x0A, 0x0C and 0x0D; 0x0A to 0x0C matches the unit's own upgrade; 0x08 has 980-byte tracks. `[hw]` / `[doc]` {synpat-1124}

text: Never commit firmware - no `.syx`, extracted sections, `.bin` images, built `.elemod` files or anything derived from a stock OS; run `git status` to check. Never weaken a check to make a test pass: the checks in `syx.verify`, `elemod` and `link` protect users (bootloader stays stock, mods must not collide); if a check wrongly refuses something, narrow the fix and test both sides. text: Cache config `0x414141`: 16 KiB I, DM and PM caches at the block tops. L1 blocks 0 and 3 are full. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
text: 1 GHz core (20 MHz x 100 / 2), 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz = 1,500 blocks/s = 666,667 cycles/block. This is confirmed on a real DT2 by the owner's idle counter. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
text: DN2 has 16 voice slots chosen at note-on, not tied to tracks, so it has no fixed stereo pair. DT2 has 32 voices: even = L, odd = R. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
text: digikit's run-time limits (its own, not the firmware's): 8 modules, 4 FX slots (3 since 2026-11-15, CONFLICTS O27 `[?]`), 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2) DSP area in 64-byte granules, 64 KiB per module file (128 KiB since 2026-11-20, the upload stage buffer `stage_bytes` on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt; `[doc]` {digikit-1120}). The firmware would allow about 900 / 450 KiB. Every limit was filled in the emulator and the next module was refused with a clean error. `[emu]` {digikit-f57}

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
text: digikit's planning budget (2026-11-14): a selection must fit 85 % of the 666,667-cycle block after the stock baseline, with emulator instruction counts projected to cycles by a high factor: that leaves 194,244 instructions per block on the DT2 and 92,796 on the DN2 (12,140 and 5,799 per voice at 16 voices). These are planning instructions, not the cycles measured free on a unit, so do not compare them with the `[hw]` headroom figures directly. On DN2 1.12 the whole DSP ran 332,039 instructions per block in the emulator with one note playing (stock baseline 334,529); the DT2 stock baseline is about 211,000. `[doc]` / `[emu]` {digikit-budget}

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: Call: `CALL (linked, delayed)` (Type 25a). Prologue `I7 = MODIFY(I7, -N)`, saves to `DM(I6 - n)`. Return `I12 = DM(I6, M7); JUMP (M14, I12) (DB)` with `RFRAME` in the delay slot.

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: Arguments R4, R8, R12, then the stack (`DM(I6, M6)`). Result in R0 (F0; R0:R1 for 64-bit). Render kernels return nothing and write through pointers.

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: Callee-saved: R3, R5-R7, R9-R11, R13-R15, I0-I3, I5, M1-M3, B3.

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: Constant registers that voice code never writes: M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0, M14 = 1, M15 = -1. Indirect jumps use DAG2 (`JUMP (M13, I12)` relies on M13 = 0). The stock interrupt code also reads B7, L6 and L7 (a valid linear stack in I7, L6 = L7 = 0) and IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT and FLAGS at any instruction; never write them, even with a save and restore (digikit finding 130, [digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md section 7](../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md)). `[doc]` {digikit-1116}

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: The exception is the float divide `0x1c06ba` (plain CALL, R4/R8 in, F0 out). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: Parameters: the ColdFire smooths them (one-pole) before the frame. The DSP converts s16 to float once per block (scale 1/32512) and ramps per sample by (new - old)/32 inside a block (/64 in DN2 FM operators).

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
text: DT2 sample machines and DN2 FM TONE render 64 samples at 96 kHz and decimate to 32 with a half-band filter.

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
text: At H2/H3 SIMD is off and no DO loop is active. The stock FX state lives in DDR: chorus `0x80459388`, delay `0x8005912c` (rings of 524,288 floats, max 8 s), reverb `0x80000018`. FX rings wrap by index arithmetic; FX units never write B or L registers, but the voice renderer does and restores them. Static FX cost: chorus 7.1k, delay 6.0k, reverb 17.2k instructions per block. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
text: The stock machines share almost no code (each machine is one large function). Only the post-voice chain and a few maths helpers are shared between DT2 and DN2. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Clock and block: 1 GHz, 32 samples per block, 666,667 cycles nominal. Measured median per block: DT2 666,582, DN2 666,784 (digikit); DN2 666,706 (elekloader's idle-task meter); the owner's idle counter on a DT2 agrees. {digikit-f103} {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Core behaviour: 59 value items (saturation with MODE1.ALUSAT, the short and multifunction compute forms, float rounding) and all cycle snippets equal, including the L2 conflict loads (2,769 vs 2,803 cycles for 4,096 loads); the 6,694 RECIPS/RSQRTS seed results are equal. So the cycle budget of rule A35 and the float rules in [`../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md`](../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md) section 6 hold on both. {digikit-f103} {digikit-f102}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Core registers set by the boot code: IMASK, MODE2, SHDBG_REVID, cache configuration (`SHL1C_CFG`) read the same on both. The traps armed (illegal opcode, L1 parity) are therefore the same. {digikit-f103}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Never store a DAG register through its own DAG (rule A33): hung a DT2 (Plaits port, digikit's "rung C"); the DN2 skill names the same pattern "the root cause of silent units" on its unit. {dt2-plaits} {dn2-skill-sharc}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Hardware loop ends in 48-bit ISA (rule A45): a DT2 froze at boot from a compressed loop end; stock DN2 1.11 obeys the rule in all 286 loops and the DN2 skill enforces it. {digikit-f91} {dn2-skill-scripts}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Decoded section 7 under 1 MiB (rule A46): the same 828-byte staging routine on DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12; the overrun crashed a DT2. {digikit-f06} {dt2-lab-capicola}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: NaN or Inf in stock FX feedback silences everything until reboot: on a DT2 from an LFO at large depth on TUNE (digikit) and in the owner's builds; on a DN2 from never-written DDR, which powers on as garbage such as `0xFFFFFFFF` (the DN2 skill). Same failure, two triggers: guard every value you feed into a feedback path, and fill new DDR in emulator tests with `0xFFFFFFFF`. {digikit-f51} {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Shared stock DSP code, by the bytes: the DT2's six wavetable render stages are in the DN2 image too. Three are byte-identical; in the other three every differing byte is a PC-relative call offset (same target) or one table-pointer literal. All call the same reciprocal helper at sw `0x1c06ba` in both images (RECIPS plus Newton steps, the helper behind A35's divide cost). A fix or measurement on one of these stages carries over. `[doc]` {digikit-f11}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: The unused frame tail carries DSP code on both (+23 instructions per block on DT2, +26 on DN2). `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: SIMD loads and stores into L2 byte space hang the DSP (DT2, Plaits port; rule A33's second half). No DN2 report either way. {dt2-plaits}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: Instruction-cache misses are the largest stall class (33 % on the DT2 Plaits models), and L2 data lines 16 KiB apart thrash the 16 KiB cache. digikit's DN2 cycle snippets match, so plan DN2 kernels the same way. {dt2-plaits} {digikit-f103}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: ILOPI catches encodings the toolchain accepts (negative shift immediates, a 48-bit form of selas): seen on DN2 units. The DT2's IMASK is the same, and 70b185's DT2 rules already forbid the same encodings. {dn2-dspstop} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: L1 block 2 holds the PM data cache, so it is not free even though the image leaves it empty (DN2). The cache configuration register is the same on the DT2. {dn2-dspstop} {digikit-f103}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: The IIR0 and FIR0 accelerators compute in a different order from the hardware reference (IIR0 output from stored word 5, FIR0 sums added in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round in ACM). Read on a DN2; neither stock engine uses them. {dn2-accel}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
text: DM and PM data caches are not coherent on DDR (a DN2 finding, applied as a rule on the DT2 without a DT2 test). `[doc]` {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: Reply record: on the DT2 the SHARC writes two copies (`0x266220`, `0x267220`, picked by a selector), words 1-6 are rewritten by firmware and words 670-676 arrive untouched. On the DN2, reply word 2 is free on 1.12 (elekloader). These allocation results have not been checked on the other device; the record addresses differ with the image. {own-dt2-notes} {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: Diagnostic reply publication: digikit's DT2 probe received 0 in 3,995 of 4,000 diagnostic word-25 records. `[hw]` Its own `core/fx` and `core/dsp-voice` clears overwrote the previous block's reply word; removing those clears restored delivery in the DN2 1.12 emulator. The replacement keeps a static word and publishes at block tail. `[emu]` Finding 101 leaves silicon DMA timing unmeasured and says the new design had not yet run on a real DT2; it does not attribute the clears to stock firmware. {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: Free L2: DT2 problems start past `0x200f5a74` on a unit, although the static map shows free space up to `0x200fa000`. DN2: usable `0x20088400-0x200b0000` per the DN2 skill, and one block in L2 stopped a unit from starting. The two stock images load different amounts into L2 (`0x2001ab7c` vs `0x2008823c`), so each device needs its own limit. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: Code in L2 "dead" stock FX spots stopped a DN2 at random moments (Digiwerk SC01); no DT2 test of the same idea. {dn2-cfw-roadmap}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: Per-sample stores into a stock DDR output buffer crashed a DT2; render into L2 and copy once. No DN2 test. {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
text: The FreeRTOS layout (idle task, unused priorities 2-4 and 6) was measured on the DT2. The DN2 image has the same FreeRTOS files, but the addresses must be re-found. {own-dt2-notes} {digikit-sharcmap}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: DSP DDR: on the DN2, `0x80531000-0xa0000000` (~507 MB) was never written in a fill-and-scan test on a unit. On the DT2 that range is the sample pool: its window runs from `0x8422b9c8` to `0x9d22b9c8`. Do not carry the DN2's "free DDR" over to the DT2. The DT2's SHARC image also zero-fills 32 MiB at `0x80a00000` and a `0x1c4`-byte control block at `0x82a00000` that the DN2 image lacks, and the SHARC functions that use them have no DN2 twin. {dn2-ddr} {dt2-lab-flex-mem} {dn2-drive}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: How stock spends the block: the DN2 engine renders every voice every block (~63-65 % flat by dnfw's idle-task method, a held voice adds ~8k cycles; elekloader reads ~80 %, conflict O15). The DT2 engine scales with what plays and governs its own load: with 8 heavy tracks it ran at 99-100 % for whole windows and missed no block. Budgets measured on one device say nothing about the other. {dn2-sharcload} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: What an overrun does: on the DT2 a late block is exactly one missed block, and even 54 provoked misses did not leave lasting damage. dn2mk2 users saw custom-voice overruns on the DN2 cut all audio until a power cycle. These are not the same experiment (sustained overload by added voices vs. single late blocks), so they do not contradict each other. A test that settles it: provoke single late blocks on a DN2 the way the DT2 test did. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: Reply word 0: on the DT2 it is a true load figure, about 6.5k cycles below an idle-task measure. On the DN2 the DN2 skill uses it as the DSP load, while dnfw reads the frame handler's own count (~416k cycles) from it. Compare both methods on one DN2 before using word 0 there. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-emulators} {dn2-sharcload}

Nine of the 23 repos ship agent instruction files (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`). `[?]`

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / How agents are used (as described)
text: Agents scan thousands of decompiled functions, infer roles (MIDI parsing, voice allocation), label symbols and draft hooks; they struggle on older DSP chips with little training data (hallucination risk). Developers run the real firmware in desktop emulators and let agents compile, boot, check for crashes and iterate many times per hour without touching hardware. `[?]` {dubspot}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / How agents are used (as described)
text: Disclosure practices: Felucca credits agents for code, tests, docs and maintenance; Schwung describes its code as largely agent-written under human review, requires AI-usage disclosure from contributors and bans Grok-generated pull requests; DT-FM and DNX disclose LLM use. elk-herd rejects AI-generated issues/PRs outright. `[doc]` {dubspot} {dt-fm} {dnx-page} {elk-herd}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / How agents are used (as described)
text: Agent files as "trap registers": examples quoted - the OLED y-axis runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader's `ev_draw` doc also says y=0 is the bottom row), and compiling ColdFire code with `-O2` without `-fno-ipa-sra` corrupts interrupt pointers. The repo that carries the second one is not named in the article. Treat both as rules to copy into any ColdFire/OLED work. `[?]` {dubspot} {elekloader-adapting}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
text: Bricking is usually recoverable when the bootloader is untouched; the danger is projects that modify boot code or lack a documented recovery path. Subtle DSP/bus timing bugs are more likely to ruin a session than bricking. One mod developer bricked an Akai MPC Sample in September (video). Verified bricks in the wave are described as rare. `[?]`

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
text: Version lock-in: each mod targets exactly one OS build; official updates break mods until ported. Abandoned solo repos leave users stuck on old builds. Web patchers and installers run with full privileges and are rarely audited. `[?]`

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
text: Elektron's 16 Sep policy bans sharing/requesting/linking to firmware mods, tools, repos or guides on Elektronauts and its social channels; a next-day amendment extended it to discontinued legacy machines; general discussion stays allowed; development moved to Discord, independent forums and GitHub (see the policy page itself in AGENT-RULES B4). `[doc]` {elektronauts-policy}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
text: Developers distribute patches or scripts, not firmware, and warn users not to share compiled `.syx`/`.bin` outputs. The article cites US DMCA section 1201 exemptions (research, repair, interoperability; active through October 2027, generally not distribution) and the EU Software Directive's narrow interoperability allowance; neither has been tested over a music-hardware mod. Paid firmware (Groove OS, $29) and unlocking paid features on current hardware raise legal risk; first takedowns are expected for commercial mods. Warranty: expect denial for faults caused by third-party firmware, depending on country. `[?]` {dubspot}

text: Elektron no longer lists old firmware; its stated reason is that downgrading can cause errors (new projects incompatible with old OS versions); the official way to ask for older versions is email. Links were deleted or rate-limited soon after being posted; a community archive.org collection exists and is incomplete (no Model: device firmware). Hosting rule on that forum: no `.syx` uploads, no private distribution, only official links. No hashes are provided in the thread. Practical rule for agents: tell users to keep their own stock files; never assume an old OS can be fetched later. `[doc]` {em-firmware-list}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: Tool: build `make`; Linux/macOS native, Windows via WSL (work in the Linux home directory, a filename in the tool repo contains `?`). Commands: `-i` summary + checksum check, `-v` detail, `-o dir` extract all, `-d ID` extract one section, `-c ID file -o new.syx` replace a section and repack, `-r` repack unchanged (self-test), `-V` version string, `-l 0..3` compression level, `--emit-container`. Sound/pattern/project dumps are `.syx` too but the tool rejects them as non-firmware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. Section 3 (MAIN OS) is the usual target; leave 2 (bootstrap) and 4 (updater) alone because the bootloader holds the recovery menu; section 8 appears as `?` (no known name); section IDs differ on other devices, so `-i` is authoritative. `.raw` sections are copied as-is, `.bin` sections are decompressed. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

text: Editing rules: overwrite bytes only, the file size must not change (later addresses shift); replacement text must be the same length and use characters already present; keep the terminating zero byte; always edit a copy in `work/` and keep `extracted/` untouched; verify with `cmp -l` (exactly the intended number of changed bytes) and by re-extracting section 3 from the new file and comparing it byte-for-byte; `-V` must not exceed the original version string length (e.g. 4 characters like `1.11`). The repacked file is smaller than Elektron's because the tool compresses slightly better (level 3 took ~14 s, level 0 is ~18x faster and ~3 % larger). The author states the worked example (replacing "UNTITLED" with "ELEKMODS") was not tested on hardware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old}

text: What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Compression: each section is raw or aPLib-variant compressed (not flagged - inferred by whether the bytes depack): LZ77 with interlaced Elias-gamma codes, a biased offset, a last-offset reuse code and a length bonus for far matches, minimum match 2; Elektron's streams keep the furthest match within 1 MiB and the longest at 2,048 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: DN1 vs DN2: bootstrap load address DN2 `0x02000000` / DN1 `0x02000800`; blob (id 7) compressed on DN2, raw on DN1; boot (id 6) absent on DN2, present (raw) on DN1; section 5 (meta) is 15 bytes, stored raw, no destination address, identical size on both; section 8 appears in OS 1.11 compressed (it is the Outbox 8 accessory firmware). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: After patching, recompute: re-encoded section data and its stream length/sum (+ padding to 4 bytes, table length includes the padding), section table offsets/lengths and 16-byte placement (and the count if sections change), the preamble (container size, content checksum), SysEx packet checksums/counters/packet count, and on DN2 the HMAC over everything before the trailer. The page does not say whether the product code, build string or version string must change, nor whether ids must be renumbered. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
text: Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing}
